Purpose: Non-equity claims provide deductions in a consistent enterprise-to-equity bridge.
Conditions: Match debt, leases, pensions and minority claims to the cash-flow perimeter.

Purpose: Relevant excess cash and non-operating assets provide additions in the enterprise-to-equity bridge.
Conditions: Only add assets excluded from the operating valuation and available to the relevant claim.

Purpose: Financial goals and their timing inform personal investment selection and asset allocation.
Conditions: Also consider liquidity, risk capacity and protection needs.

Purpose: Asset allocation provides target exposures and constraints for portfolio construction.
NAV, expense ratios and tracking differences help assess fund implementation and investor outcomes.
Conditions: Use the appropriate fund structure and benchmark.

Purpose: The accounting equation makes funding claims reconcile with the asset side.
Conditions: Use total liabilities and equity, not share capital alone.

Purpose: Double entry lets one transaction be traced through accounts and statements.
Accrual accounting permits revenue and customer receivables before collection.
Conditions: Recognition criteria must first be met.

Purpose: A qualifying sale on credit records revenue and a customer receivable.
Conditions: A cash sale does not create an outstanding receivable.

Purpose: Operating receivables are one component of operating working capital.
Conditions: Exclude non-operating receivables when defining the operating perimeter.

Purpose: Operating inventory is included in operating working capital.
Operating supplier payables reduce operating working capital.
Increases in operating working capital generally reduce operating cash flow in the indirect reconciliation.
Conditions: Hold other cash-flow components fixed and apply the reporting framework.

Purpose: Receivable days relate customer balances to a consistent credit-sales denominator.
Conditions: Use average balances and matched periods when available.

Purpose: Inventory days relate inventory balances to the appropriate cost-of-sales denominator.
Conditions: Match inventory valuation and reporting periods.

Purpose: Payable days relate supplier balances to relevant purchases or a documented cost proxy.
Conditions: Credit purchases are preferred where available.

Purpose: Inventory days plus receivable days less payable days gives the cash conversion cycle.
Conditions: Keep day-count and denominator conventions consistent.

Purpose: Credit terms and collections influence the amount and timing of customer receivables.
Supplier payment terms influence payable balances and payment timing.
Factoring and invoice discounting can provide funding against receivables.
Conditions: Derecognition, recourse and classification depend on the arrangement.

Purpose: Supply-chain finance changes supplier payment and buyer funding arrangements.
Conditions: Assess substance, balance-sheet classification and required disclosures.

Purpose: Uncollected customer balances may require an expected credit-loss allowance.
Conditions: Framework and estimation inputs determine the recognised allowance.

Purpose: Credit-loss expense can reduce reported profit without a contemporaneous cash payment.
Depreciation reduces EBIT for depreciating operating assets.
Non-cash depreciation deducted in operating profit is added back in the standard FCFF build.
Conditions: Avoid adding it twice; account for associated reinvestment separately.

Purpose: Cash operating capital expenditure is deducted when calculating standard FCFF.
Conditions: Keep acquisitions and non-operating investments explicitly classified.

Purpose: An increase in operating working capital is deducted in the standard FCFF build.
Conditions: Use change in the balance, not the full closing balance.

Purpose: Operating earnings provide the profit base for after-tax operating profit.
Conditions: A simple EBIT times one-minus-tax-rate model is an assumption, not a universal tax rule.

Purpose: NOPAT is a starting point for FCFF before non-cash adjustments and reinvestment.
FCFF is discounted at a matching WACC in a standard enterprise DCF.
Conditions: Risk, currency, nominal/real basis and tax treatment must align.

Purpose: FCFE is discounted at a matching cost of equity.
Conditions: Do not discount equity cash flows at WACC.

Purpose: Net borrowing is included in a conventional FCFE reconciliation.
Conditions: Other financing claims and lease treatment must be consistent.

Purpose: Financing debt proceeds and principal repayments do not form operating FCFF.
Conditions: Debt can change risk, tax shields and value through financing channels.

Purpose: An enterprise DCF discounts future FCFF and a consistent terminal value.
An equity DCF discounts future FCFE and an equity-consistent terminal value.
Discounted operating FCFF estimates the specified operating enterprise value.
Conditions: Adjust separately for excluded non-operating assets and claims.

Purpose: The enterprise-to-equity bridge reconciles operating value to shareholder value.
The bridge adds relevant non-operating assets and removes non-equity claims.
Conditions: Use a consistent definition; avoid double counting cash, leases and minorities.

Purpose: Cash is assessed for operating need before it is treated as excess cash.
Conditions: Not all balance-sheet cash is freely distributable.

Purpose: Restricted cash affects whether balances can be added as available excess cash.
Debt may be deducted in the enterprise-to-equity bridge.
Conditions: Use the valuation perimeter and market value where appropriate.

Purpose: Lease liabilities may be treated as debt-like claims in valuation.
Conditions: Cash-flow and EBITDA treatment must match that decision.

Purpose: Non-controlling interests reconcile consolidated operating value to parent equity.
Conditions: Match the consolidated cash-flow perimeter.

Purpose: Pension deficits can represent claims on enterprise value.
Conditions: Apply tax and perimeter conventions consistently.

Purpose: Reinvestment and incremental operating returns connect growth to value creation.
ROIC above a comparable cost of capital is a value-creation diagnostic.
Conditions: Use forward economics and matching capital/risk definitions; one historical spread is not proof.

Purpose: Terminal growth must be supported by reinvestment and sustainable returns.
A growing perpetuity provides a common terminal-value formula.
Conditions: Requires a discount rate above growth and a credible stable-growth state.

Purpose: Discount the terminal value along with explicit forecast cash flows.
Mid-year and stub-period conventions reflect cash-flow timing.
Conditions: State whether timing conventions apply to the terminal value as well.

Purpose: Sensitivity, scenario and reverse-DCF analysis expose valuation uncertainty.
Comparing market price and estimated value shapes an investment thesis.
Peer selection requires accounting and economic comparability.
Earnings per share is the denominator of a share-price P/E ratio.
Conditions: Use matched trailing or forward periods and attributable diluted earnings.

Purpose: Equity book value contributes to price-to-book comparisons.
Conditions: Use common equity and a consistent per-share or aggregate basis.

Purpose: Revenue provides the denominator for EV/revenue.
EBITDA and EBIT provide operating earnings denominators for enterprise multiples.
Conditions: Normalise leases and non-recurring items consistently.

Purpose: Enterprise multiples use enterprise value rather than common equity value.
Equity multiples value the equity claim; enterprise multiples value a broader claim.
Forward multiples use forward earnings or other forecast measures.
Conditions: The price date and forecast period must be explicit.

Purpose: Growth, risk and returns help explain differences in comparable multiples.
Sum-of-the-parts valuation uses segment economics and appropriate segment methods.
Comparable deals provide evidence for transaction valuation.
Conditions: Deal premiums and synergies need separate interpretation.

Purpose: Control and liquidity characteristics affect negotiation and transaction pricing.
Conditions: Do not automatically add a control premium to value already including control improvements.

Purpose: Capital expenditure is distinguished from current operating expense.
Capitalising expenditure can replace an immediate expense with later depreciation or amortisation.
Conditions: Capitalisation must meet the reporting rules.

Purpose: Depreciable PPE is allocated to expense over useful lives.
Conditions: Land and some other asset components require separate treatment.

Purpose: Completed qualifying construction can transfer from capital work in progress to PPE.
Conditions: Depreciation generally begins when ready for intended use.

Purpose: Right-of-use assets arise from applicable lease accounting.
Lease liabilities represent recognised lease-payment obligations.
Goodwill and other intangibles require applicable impairment assessment.
Conditions: Amortisation and testing differ by asset and framework.

Purpose: Purchase-price allocation recognises acquired assets, liabilities and possible goodwill.
Acquisition accounting feeds the pro-forma merger model.
Consolidation combines controlled entities and eliminates intercompany amounts.
The equity method can record the investor share of associate or joint-venture results.
Conditions: Presentation and eligibility depend on the reporting framework.

Purpose: Share-based compensation creates expense and potential equity dilution.
Temporary differences and eligible tax losses can create deferred tax balances.
Conditions: Recognition and recoverability require applicable criteria.

Purpose: Differences between tax and book recognition produce some deferred tax effects.
Tax depreciation affects operating cash taxes separately from book depreciation.
Usable tax losses can change forecast cash taxes.
Conditions: Availability and utilisation limits are jurisdiction-specific.

Purpose: The tax benefit of interest depends on tax capacity and deduction rules.
Conditions: A stated tax rate alone does not prove a usable tax shield.

Purpose: APV can separate operating value from the value of financing side effects.
Usable debt interest deductions affect conventional after-tax WACC.
CAPM is one model used to estimate the cost of equity.
Risk-free rate and equity risk premium are CAPM inputs.
Equity beta measures market-related exposure in CAPM.
Conditions: Historical estimates have noise and specification limitations.

Purpose: Unlevering and relevering translate beta across capital structures.
Conditions: Debt risk and tax assumptions matter.

Purpose: Bottom-up beta combines comparable business risk with a target capital structure.
Debt required return and applicable tax treatment enter WACC.
Market-value capital weights enter WACC.
Country risk and currency choice affect an international cost-of-capital estimate.
Credit quality and leverage help assess distress risk and financing spreads.
Incremental project cash flows are discounted to calculate project NPV.
Relevant cash flows include opportunity costs but exclude sunk costs.
Equivalent annual cost can compare repeatable alternatives of different lives.
Conditions: Only where replacement and risk assumptions support the comparison.

Purpose: IRR and NPV can rank projects differently due to scale, timing and reinvestment assumptions.
Managerial flexibility has option-like payoffs.
Conditions: Real options are not identical to freely traded financial options.

Purpose: Payout decisions are implemented through dividends and share repurchases.
Acquisitions and organic investment are alternative routes for deploying capital.
Capital allocation can be assessed through operating returns and value created.
Fixed and variable costs determine contribution and break-even volume.
Price, volume and mix explain changes in revenue.
Fixed operating costs and utilisation contribute to operating leverage.
Lifetime customer contribution is compared with acquisition cost.
Conditions: Match cohorts, contribution definitions and discounting conventions.

Purpose: Retention, churn and customer behaviour affect lifetime-value assumptions.
Working-capital and asset intensity influence the reinvestment needed for growth.
Operating drivers become revenue and cost schedules in a financial model.
Operating forecasts supply model assumptions and schedules.
Variance analysis diagnoses differences between forecasts and actual results.
Costing methods affect measured product and customer profitability.
Relevant costs and contribution support make-or-buy decisions.
Conditions: Consider opportunity cost and avoid irrelevant allocated costs.

Purpose: Capacity and product-mix decisions can use constrained optimisation.
Internal transfer-pricing decisions differ from tax compliance transfer pricing.
Conditions: Both may use similar transaction data but have different objectives and constraints.

Purpose: A three-statement model connects transaction effects across the statements.
Working-capital schedules forecast operating balances and their cash-flow changes.
Fixed-asset schedules link capex, disposals and depreciation.
Debt schedules forecast debt drawdowns, repayments and interest.
Tax schedules distinguish applicable current taxes and deferred tax effects.
Interest and cash or debt funding can create circular model dependencies.
Conditions: Resolve deliberately rather than silently relying on unstable iteration.

Purpose: Scenario and sensitivity models explore valuation and financing assumptions.
Merger modelling combines standalone forecasts, terms, financing and adjustments.
LBO models connect purchase price, debt, operating cash flow and exit equity.
Project models support debt sizing and repayment sculpting.
Reproducibility and checks support model auditability.
Liquidity ratios help assess the need for buffers and contingency funding.
Conditions: Ratios alone do not describe cash timing or facility availability.

Purpose: Margins can be decomposed using cost behaviour and contribution economics.
Turnover metrics indicate the operating capital used to support sales.
Leverage and coverage metrics inform repayment capacity and covenant analysis.
DuPont analysis decomposes ROE into profitability, turnover and leverage.
Conditions: Choose a consistent three-part or extended specification.

Purpose: Sustainable growth links profitability, retention and financing assumptions.
Normalisation supports comparable valuation denominators.
Cyclical peaks and troughs affect earnings and valuation comparisons.
Revenue-quality analysis tests whether recognition reflects applicable criteria.
Forensic analysis tests whether capitalisation improperly delays expense.
Provision and reserve movements can affect reported earnings.
Accrual quality is assessed partly by reconciling earnings to operating cash.
Unusual receivables can signal collection, recognition or credit problems.
Conditions: A warning sign is a prompt for investigation, not proof of fraud.

Purpose: Unusual inventory may indicate demand, costing or write-down problems.
Classification choices can change presented operating cash flow.
Conditions: Distinguish permitted framework differences from manipulation.

Purpose: Guarantees and commitments can create exposure beyond recorded debt.
Auditor findings can reveal weaknesses, uncertainty or reporting qualifications.
Footnote investigation uses annual reports and other filings.
An IPO can provide a startup or private investor exit route.
Conditions: Lockups and retained ownership can limit immediate liquidity.

Purpose: Equity markets operate through exchanges and intermediaries.
Index membership and weights affect index-tracking portfolios.
Order choices interact with the order book, spreads and liquidity.
Short selling commonly requires borrowing securities.
Conditions: Rules, borrow availability and margin requirements vary.

Purpose: Fundamental analysis uses statement analysis and peer context.
Competitive advantage helps assess the duration of excess operating returns.
Investment theses should be compared with subsequent evidence and outcomes.
Ownership concentration and pledged shares can introduce specific governance or financing risks.
Coupon and principal conventions define bond cash flows.
Present-value calculations provide the basic bond-pricing framework.
A matching spot curve discounts each bond cash flow separately.
Bootstrapping infers discount factors from suitable instrument prices.
Duration measures local bond-price sensitivity to a specified yield change.
Conditions: Effective duration accounts for cash-flow changes where relevant.

Purpose: Convexity supplements first-order duration estimates.
Credit spreads reflect default risk along with liquidity and other premiums.
Conditions: A spread is not a pure probability-of-default estimate.

Purpose: Floating coupons reset against specified reference-rate conventions.
Callable, puttable and convertible bonds contain option-like features.
Collateral, seniority and covenants affect credit protection and recovery.
Immunisation and bond ladders can support liability-oriented portfolios.
Conditions: Immunisation assumptions and rebalancing needs must be explicit.

Purpose: Currency forwards and futures can hedge specified currency exposures.
Conditions: Basis, timing and counterparty constraints remain.

Purpose: Option positions can be represented through payoff and profit diagrams.
Conditions: Profit includes premium and other relevant costs.

Purpose: Moneyness and value components describe option positions.
Put-call parity is an arbitrage relationship under its assumptions.
Conditions: Match exercise style, maturity, financing and distributions.

Purpose: Binomial pricing uses possible future states and risk-neutral valuation.
Option pricing uses volatility assumptions.
Conditions: Model assumptions limit applicability; implied volatility is model-derived.

Purpose: Greeks support management of local option risk exposures.
Conditions: Sensitivities change with price, time and volatility.

Purpose: Swaps can alter interest-rate, currency or commodity exposure.
Credit derivatives transfer specified credit-event exposure.
Conditions: Basis, contract definition and counterparty risk matter.

Purpose: Caps, floors and swaptions contain interest-rate option payoffs.
Structured notes combine funding instruments and contingent payoffs.
Clearing and collateral mitigate some counterparty exposure.
Conditions: They do not eliminate every market, liquidity or operational risk.

Purpose: A hedge may leave residual basis exposure.
Correlation helps explain diversification benefits.
Conditions: Correlation can change, especially under stress.

Purpose: Mean-variance optimisation produces a model efficient frontier.
Conditions: Expected returns, covariances and constraints drive the result.

Purpose: Portfolio factor models extend the analysis of common return exposures.
An investment policy statement guides allocation and implementation.
Risk capacity and horizon affect retirement investment choices.
